blocks.x: How IoT, Twin & Robotics lands in Capabilities — the constraints that shape the build, the gated delivery pattern, and the deltas we commit against your baseline.

In Technology & SaaS, iot, digital twin & robotics bridges the physical and digital enterprise: industrial sensor network, digital twin platforms, computer vision and edge ai, predictive maintenance, robotics and autonomous systems integration, connected products, and smart infrastructure. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: industrial iot & sensor network, digital twin platform engineering, computer vision & edge ai — delivered on Dataq Twinverse and Dataq Nexus with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Velocity vs. reliability tension
Deploy frequency rises while incident load eats roadmap; error budgets exist in slide decks, not in release policy.

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: EU AI Act (as AI providers) and Sector overlays (PCI, HIPAA B2B). Compliance duties inherited from enterprise customers. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Programs run on the fixed rhythm below, chosen so progress is legible from week one. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
